contract_plain_english: With the state vector ordered as q = (p,u)^T, the linear acoustics equations are exactly q_t + A q_x = 0 for A with rows (0,K) and (1/rho,0). Expanding the first row gives the pressure equation and expanding the second gives the velocity equation. The constants and state order are essential.

conclusions: The acoustics equations p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0 can be written as q_t + A q_x = 0 with the displayed q and A.
Conversely, expanding the two rows of q_t + A q_x = 0 yields exactly those two component equations.
definitions_and_conventions: Vectors are columns and the state order is pressure first, velocity second.
The derivative q_x is taken componentwise, so A q_x has components K u_x and (1/rho) p_x.
The matrix is constant because K and rho are assumed constant in this linear model.
hypotheses: K and rho are constant material coefficients.
rho is nonzero so that the matrix entry 1/rho is defined.
p and u have the first partial derivatives appearing in the system.
implicit_context: The quantities and matrix entries are real.
Physical density and bulk modulus are positive in the intended acoustics model, although only rho != 0 is algebraically necessary for this matrix rewrite.
The matrix equation is a repackaging of the two displayed PDEs, not a discretization or an approximate relation.

details: q must be ordered as (p,u), not (u,p).
With that order, K occupies the upper-right entry and 1/rho the lower-left entry.
The first matrix row is p_t + K u_x = 0.
The second matrix row is u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0.

undebatable_constraints: Use q = (p,u)^T in that exact order.
Use A = [[0,K],[1/rho,0]] with zero diagonal entries.
State q_t + A q_x = 0, not q_t + (Aq)_x = 0 as the displayed equation, even though constant A makes them related.
Preserve exact row-by-row correspondence with both equations in (1.5).
Treat K and rho as constants and ensure 1/rho is defined.
